import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.20

by A. I. Kokorin

Does the class of orderable groups coincide with the smallest axiomatizable class
containing pro-orderable groups? (See 1.35.)

All orders on a group are two-sided invariant here: a *partial order* of a group $G$ is a
partial order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies $xa \le xb$ and $ax \le bx$ for all
$a, b, x \in G$. A group is *orderable* if it admits a linear order of this kind. Following
Problem 1.35, a group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group) if each of its partial orders can
be extended to a linear order.

A class of groups is *axiomatizable* if it is the class of all models of some set of
first-order sentences in the language of groups (with symbols for multiplication, inversion
and the identity). The smallest axiomatizable class containing a class $K$ of groups is the
class of models of the first-order theory of $K$, i.e. of all sentences true in every group
of $K$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language
namespace Kourovka.«3.20»

def IsBiInvariant {G : Type*} [Group G] (le : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ a b x : G, le a b → le (x * a) (x * b)) ∧ (∀ a b x : G, le a b → le (a * x) (b * x))
blocks.docstring:
A binary relation `le` on a group is *two-sided invariant* if `le a b` implies
`le (x * a) (x * b)` and `le (a * x) (b * x)` for all `x`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«3.20».IsBiInvariant
justification.why_needed: Two-sided invariance of a relation on a group, `Covariant G G (· * ·) r ∧ Covariant G G (swap (· * ·)) r`; needed because Mathlib's ordered-group classes (`IsOrderedMonoid`, `GroupCone`, `LinearOrderedCommGroup`) require commutativity, and `MulLeftMono`/`MulRightMono` are tied to an `LE` instance rather than an arbitrary relation.

blocks.name: IsBiInvariant
blocks.text:
/-- A binary relation `le` on a group is *two-sided invariant* if `le a b` implies
`le (x * a) (x * b)` and `le (a * x) (b * x)` for all `x`. -/
def IsBiInvariant {G : Type*} [Group G] (le : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ a b x : G, le a b → le (x * a) (x * b)) ∧ (∀ a b x : G, le a b → le (a * x) (b * x))

blocks.code:
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ l : LinearOrder G, IsBiInvariant l.le
blocks.docstring: A group is *orderable* if it admits a two-sided invariant linear order.

justification.name: Kourovka.«3.20».IsOrderable
justification.why_needed: 'Orderable group' = admits a linear order invariant under left and right multiplication. Mathlib's `IsOrderedMonoid` requires commutativity, so the bi-invariance is expressed with `MulLeftMono ∧ MulRightMono` over an existentially quantified `LinearOrder`.

blocks.name: IsOrderable

blocks.docstring:
A group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group) if every two-sided invariant partial order
on it can be extended to a two-sided invariant linear order.

justification.closest_existing_considered: none (searched Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for orderable/bi-order notions)
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.20».IsProOrderable
justification.why_needed: Kokorin's 'pro-orderable' (O*-group, Problem 1.35): every bi-invariant partial order of the group extends to a bi-invariant linear order. No Mathlib/repo counterpart.

blocks.name: IsProOrderable
blocks.text:
/-- A group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group) if every two-sided invariant partial order
on it can be extended to a two-sided invariant linear order. -/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ p : PartialOrder G, IsBiInvariant p.le →
    ∃ l : LinearOrder G, IsBiInvariant l.le ∧ ∀ a b : G, p.le a b → l.le a b

blocks.docstring:
A class `C` of groups is *axiomatizable* if there is a set `T` of first-order sentences

justification.name: Kourovka.«3.20».IsAxiomatizable
justification.why_needed: A class `C : Set GrpCat` of groups is axiomatizable iff `∃ T : groupLanguage.Theory, ∀ G, G ∈ C ↔ G ⊨ T`. Mathlib has `Theory.Model`, `Theory.ModelType` and `completeTheory` but no notion of an axiomatizable/elementary class.

def proOrderableTheory : groupLanguage.Theory :=
  {φ | ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], IsProOrderable H → H ⊨ φ}
blocks.docstring:
The first-order theory of the pro-orderable groups: the set of all sentences in the
language of groups that hold in every pro-orderable group. Its class of models is the
smallest axiomatizable class containing the pro-orderable groups, see
`forall_isAxiomatizable_iff_model_proOrderableTheory`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.completeTheory (theory of a single structure, not of a class)
justification.name: Kourovka.«3.20».proOrderableTheory
justification.why_needed: The first-order theory Th(K) of the class K of pro-orderable groups; its model class is the smallest axiomatizable class containing K.

theorem IsProOrderable.isOrderable {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsProOrderable G) :
    IsOrderable G := by
  obtain ⟨l, hl, -⟩ := h
    { le := (· = ·)
      le_refl := fun _ => rfl
      le_trans := fun _ _ _ => Eq.trans
      le_antisymm := fun _ _ h _ => h }
    ⟨fun _ _ _ h => congrArg _ h, fun _ _ _ h => congrArg (· * _) h⟩
  exact ⟨l, hl⟩

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem forall_isAxiomatizable_iff_model_proOrderableTheory (G : Type) [Group G] :
    (∀ C : ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], Prop, IsAxiomatizable C →
      (∀ (H : Type) [Group H], IsProOrderable H → C H) → C G) ↔
    G ⊨ proOrderableTheory := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact h (fun H _ => H ⊨ proOrderableTheory) ⟨_, fun _ _ => Iff.rfl⟩
      fun H _ hH => model_proOrderableTheory H hH
  · intro h C ⟨T, hT⟩ hC
    refine (hT G).2 ⟨fun φ hφ => h.realize_of_mem φ ?_⟩
    exact fun H _ hH => ((hT H).1 (hC H hH)).realize_of_mem φ hφ
blocks.docstring:
A group is a model of the theory of the pro-orderable groups if and only if it belongs to
every axiomatizable class of groups containing all pro-orderable groups. Hence the class of
models of `proOrderableTheory` is the smallest axiomatizable class containing the
pro-orderable groups.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question: 'orderable' means (bi-)linearly orderable groups, 'axiomatizable' means first-order (elementary) axiomatizable, so the smallest axiomatizable class containing a class K is the class of models of the first-order theory Th(K); 'pro-orderable' is Kokorin's terminology from Problem 1.35 (groups every partial order of which extends to a linear order, i.e. O*-groups), and since pro-orderable groups are orderable and orderable groups form an axiomatizable class (Łoś), the question is equivalently whether every orderable group is a model of the theory of the pro-orderable groups; the '(See 1.35.)' cross-reference adds no further question.
claims.reviewer_why: Final theorem is c05's literal class-equality statement `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (IsOrderable G ↔ G ⊨ proOrderableTheory)`, where proOrderableTheory = all group-language sentences true in every pro-orderable group (so its models form the smallest axiomatizable class containing the pro-orderable groups). Composed with c08's explicit relation-based definitions of bi-invariance / orderable / pro-orderable (clearer than c05's implicit-instance `MulLeftMono G` under `∀ p : PartialOrder G`), a global Structure instance (c05/c03), and c03's API lemma proving that being a model of proOrderableTheory is equivalent to membership in every axiomatizable class containing the pro-orderable groups, which verifies the 'smallest axiomatizable class' reading inside the file. c01 (IsLeast over Set GrpCat) and c03 (intersection form) are also faithful but heavier; c02/c04/c06/c07 state only the inclusion Orderable ⊆ Mod(Th(K)), which is equivalent via known theorems (pro-orderable ⇒ orderable; Łoś) but less literal.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.20

by A. I. Kokorin

Does the class of orderable groups coincide with the smallest axiomatizable class
containing pro-orderable groups? (See 1.35.)

All orders on a group are two-sided invariant here: a *partial order* of a group $G$ is a
partial order $\le$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies $xa \le xb$ and $ax \le bx$ for all

Problem 1.35, a group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group) if each of its partial orders can
be extended to a linear order.

A class of groups is *axiomatizable* if it is the class of all models of some set of
first-order sentences in the language of groups (with symbols for multiplication, inversion
and the identity). The smallest axiomatizable class containing a class $K$ of groups is the
class of models of the first-order theory of $K$, i.e. of all sentences true in every group
of $K$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

namespace Kourovka.«3.20»

/-- A binary relation `le` on a group is *two-sided invariant* if `le a b` implies
`le (x * a) (x * b)` and `le (a * x) (b * x)` for all `x`. -/
def IsBiInvariant {G : Type*} [Group G] (le : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ a b x : G, le a b → le (x * a) (x * b)) ∧ (∀ a b x : G, le a b → le (a * x) (b * x))

/-- A group is *orderable* if it admits a two-sided invariant linear order. -/
def IsOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ l : LinearOrder G, IsBiInvariant l.le

/-- A group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group) if every two-sided invariant partial order
on it can be extended to a two-sided invariant linear order. -/
def IsProOrderable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ p : PartialOrder G, IsBiInvariant p.le →
    ∃ l : LinearOrder G, IsBiInvariant l.le ∧ ∀ a b : G, p.le a b → l.le a b

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups: a binary multiplication,
a unary inversion and a constant for the identity. -/
inductive GroupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | mul : GroupFunc 2
  | inv : GroupFunc 1
  | one : GroupFunc 0

/-- The first-order language of groups, with function symbols `*`, `⁻¹` and `1` and no
relation symbols. -/
def groupLanguage : Language :=
  { Functions := GroupFunc
    Relations := fun _ => Empty }
  deriving Language.IsAlgebraic

/-- Every group is a structure for the language of groups, interpreting the function symbols
by the group operations. -/
instance (G : Type*) [Group G] : groupLanguage.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f := match n, f with
    | _, .mul => fun x => x 0 * x 1
    | _, .inv => fun x => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, .one => fun _ => 1

/-- A class `C` of groups is *axiomatizable* if there is a set `T` of first-order sentences
in the language of groups such that `C` consists exactly of the groups that are models
of `T`. -/
def IsAxiomatizable (C : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : groupLanguage.Theory, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], C G ↔ G ⊨ T

/-- The first-order theory of the pro-orderable groups: the set of all sentences in the
language of groups that hold in every pro-orderable group. Its class of models is the
smallest axiomatizable class containing the pro-orderable groups, see
`forall_isAxiomatizable_iff_model_proOrderableTheory`. -/
def proOrderableTheory : groupLanguage.Theory :=
  {φ | ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], IsProOrderable H → H ⊨ φ}

/-- Every pro-orderable group is orderable: extend the trivial partial order. -/
@[category API, AMS 6 20]
theorem IsProOrderable.isOrderable {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsProOrderable G) :
    IsOrderable G := by
  obtain ⟨l, hl, -⟩ := h
    { le := (· = ·)
      le_refl := fun _ => rfl
      le_trans := fun _ _ _ => Eq.trans
      le_antisymm := fun _ _ h _ => h }
    ⟨fun _ _ _ h => congrArg _ h, fun _ _ _ h => congrArg (· * _) h⟩
  exact ⟨l, hl⟩

/-- Every pro-orderable group is a model of the theory of the pro-orderable groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem model_proOrderableTheory (G : Type) [Group G] (h : IsProOrderable G) :
    G ⊨ proOrderableTheory :=
  ⟨fun _ hφ => hφ G h⟩

/-- A group is a model of the theory of the pro-orderable groups if and only if it belongs to
every axiomatizable class of groups containing all pro-orderable groups. Hence the class of
models of `proOrderableTheory` is the smallest axiomatizable class containing the
pro-orderable groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 20]
theorem forall_isAxiomatizable_iff_model_proOrderableTheory (G : Type) [Group G] :
    (∀ C : ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], Prop, IsAxiomatizable C →
      (∀ (H : Type) [Group H], IsProOrderable H → C H) → C G) ↔
    G ⊨ proOrderableTheory := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact h (fun H _ => H ⊨ proOrderableTheory) ⟨_, fun _ _ => Iff.rfl⟩
      fun H _ hH => model_proOrderableTheory H hH
  · intro h C ⟨T, hT⟩ hC
    refine (hT G).2 ⟨fun φ hφ => h.realize_of_mem φ ?_⟩
    exact fun H _ hH => ((hT H).1 (hC H hH)).realize_of_mem φ hφ

/-- The group of integers, written multiplicatively, is orderable. -/
@[category test, AMS 6 20]
theorem isOrderable_multiplicative_int : IsOrderable (Multiplicative ℤ) :=
  ⟨inferInstance, fun _ _ _ h => mul_le_mul_right h _, fun _ _ _ h => mul_le_mul_left h _⟩

@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_mul {G : Type*} [Group G] (a b : G) :
    @Structure.funMap groupLanguage G _ 2 GroupFunc.mul ![a, b] = a * b :=
  rfl

@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_inv {G : Type*} [Group G] (a : G) :
    @Structure.funMap groupLanguage G _ 1 GroupFunc.inv ![a] = a⁻¹ :=
  rfl

@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem funMap_one {G : Type*} [Group G] :
    @Structure.funMap groupLanguage G _ 0 GroupFunc.one ![] = (1 : G) :=
  rfl

/--
Does the class of orderable groups coincide with the smallest axiomatizable class
containing pro-orderable groups?

That is, is a group orderable if and only if it satisfies every first-order sentence in the
language of groups that holds in all pro-orderable groups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 6 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.20» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (IsOrderable G ↔ G ⊨ proOrderableTheory) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.20»

items: 'Smallest axiomatizable class containing K' is formalized as Mod(Th(K)) (models of the set of all group-language sentences true in every pro-orderable group), rather than literally as the intersection of all axiomatizable classes containing K; these coincide by a standard argument, as the decomposition notes state.
Language of groups chosen with symbols mul, inv, one (standard); any other standard signature for groups yields the same axiomatizable classes since inv and one are definable from mul.

'Partial order of a group' and 'linear order of a group' are taken to be two-sided invariant (a ≤ b ⇒ xa ≤ xb and ax ≤ bx), following Kokorin–Kopytov; expressed via Mathlib's `MulLeftMono` and `MulRightMono`. Extension means ≤ ⊆ ≤'.
Both the groups G under test and the pro-orderable groups H defining the theory are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following repository convention.
The statement asserts full coincidence of the two classes (an `↔` for every group G), including the direction Mod(Th(K)) ⊆ Orderable which is known to hold; this is faithful to 'coincide'.
Added two short API lemmas (pro-orderable ⇒ model of the theory; pro-orderable ⇒ orderable) and one test (ℤ is orderable) to sanity-check the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING guidance.

reviewer_notes: Single yes/no slot; all candidates formalized it and none objected to the decomposition. Interpretive choices (shared by all candidates and the decomposition notes): orders are two-sided invariant (Kokorin–Kopytov usage); 'pro-orderable' per Problem 1.35 = every bi-invariant partial order extends (as a relation) to a bi-invariant linear order; 'axiomatizable' = models of an arbitrary set of first-order sentences in the signature {*, ⁻¹, 1} (choice of signature does not affect which classes of groups are axiomatizable); all groups live in `Type`, matching the other Kourovka files. answer(True) asserts the classes coincide, answer(False) that they differ; every quantifier is after answer(sorry). Boundary: trivial group is both orderable and a model, consistent. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning and also builds under `lake --wfail build` when placed at FormalConjectures/Kourovka/3_20.lean (temporary copy removed). Bespoke first-order language of groups is kept in the problem file since Mathlib has none (only Language.ring); a maintainer may wish to move it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. The pre-existing lakefile.toml diff and run/ directory in the checkout were not touched by me.
statement: Does the class of orderable groups coincide with the smallest axiomatizable class containing pro-orderable groups? (See 1.35.)
